title: Runtime memory hedging policy for mixed-batch KV eviction
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: OOMs and tail latency spikes occur under mixed traffic where large-weight residency (multiple model variants) competes with growing KV cache and activation footprints. Current static headroom rules are either wasteful (over-reserve across tenants) or fragile (under-reserve for bursts). Goal: design and implement a runtime 'hedging' memory policy that maintains a compact, rapidly-reclaimable safety buffer per-GPU based on short-horizon demand forecasting, prioritized KV eviction, and opportunistic weight offload for cold models. The policy should reduce OOMs, limit tail latency impact, and avoid large persistent memory over-reservation. This ticket covers design, simulation, prototype implementation in the serving runtime, and an initial rollout experiment on a canary cluster.
acceptance_criteria: Hedging buffer allocator implemented in runtime and configurable via node config
Eviction order: prefix/pinned-safe eviction first, then tenant-LRU segments, with per-tenant min quotas respected
Quantile-based short-horizon predictor reduces observed OOM frequency by >= 60% on historical traces
Tail p99 token latency increase <= 5% for production mixes in canary tests
Runtime exposes telemetry: hedging_reserve_bytes, reclaimed_bytes, eviction_reasons, prediction_error_quantiles
Automated e2e regression test that simulates KV surge and verifies eviction/reclaim sequence without OOM
tasks: Design hedging allocator algorithm and formalize eviction priorities
Add runtime sensors for per-GPU live memory categories (weights/KV/activations/ephemeral)
Implement short-horizon predictor (exponential moving quantiles) and calibration hooks
Implement hedging buffer allocator and reclaimed path in runtime
Create safe offload path for idle/resident weights (cold model eviction to host memory/SSD) as optional step
Instrument telemetry and dashboards for canary cluster
Run offline simulator with Jan-Feb traces and produce results
Create rollout plan and rollback criteria for canary -> gradual rollout
notes: Key constraints: reclaim must be sub-10ms for prefix evictions to avoid user-visible stalls; weight offload is higher latency and opt-in per model.
Trade-offs: Larger hedging buffers reduce OOMs but increase steady-state memory headroom waste; predictor accuracy and correction rate are critical.
We will prioritize eviction strategies that preserve KV segments used by active prefix windows to avoid quality regressions for long-running chats.
Operator controls: global hedging factor, per-tenant min_kv_quota, eviction_mode (aggressive|balanced|conservative)
This ticket intentionally leaves long-term weight tiering (hot/cold storage policies) to a follow-up; here we implement a safe offload API.
Related research: small-scale experiments suggest quantile predictors on 10s windows outperform simple EWMA for burst detection in our traces. See design doc for plots.
